## Move H-1B Registration Intake to January 15

For the next cap season, I propose setting January 15 as our internal deadline for H-1B registration intake, with later requests handled case by case. This would give employers a clear schedule and give us more time to resolve missing information before the registration window opens. It is a service and workload improvement, not a response to clients being late: our current process is to send a questionnaire whenever an employer asks, without giving anyone a set date.

Last season, we filed 14 registrations for six employer clients, and nine of those registrations came in during the final week of February. Rosa logged roughly 11 hours of overtime the week the window opened. Much of that concentration reflects our process rather than client delay. One HR contact said she would happily have sent everything in January if we had asked. January 15 is a realistic target: HR teams are back from the holidays, budgets are set, and employers already budget for the $215-per-beneficiary registration fee in Q1.

Earlier intake also gives us a better opportunity to catch consequential errors. Brightwater Analytics sent a beneficiary’s passport scan two days before the window opened; it had expired in October, and we caught that only because Rosa checked the dates. Registration itself is straightforward, but passport errors can jeopardize the validity of a selection. We should build time for that review into the schedule rather than rely on last-minute checks.

The practical changes would be:
- Send engagement letters and a one-page questionnaire the week of December 7, clearly stating the January 15 intake deadline.
- Have Rosa own the intake tracker, with a clean six weeks after the deadline to chase gaps, confirm information, and flag unresolved issues.
- Review requests received after January 15 case by case, based on capacity and whether we can complete the necessary checks.

I’d like Marcus and me to agree on this approach Thursday so we can prepare the December letters. The message to employers would be simple: an earlier intake date helps us give each registration proper attention and resolve questions well before filing.
